scope_review.parent_objection: The firstreview rejects targets1–7 because they appear once in the Western developmental-benchmark citation cluster and calls Amsterdam1972 the original mark-test paradigm. But the abstract says this studyattempted toreplicate the FINDING thatWesternchildren show mirror self-recognition at18–24months acrosscultures, and introduction attributes that specific finding to a named setofempiricalpapers. The codebook warns against confusing the paper supplying a task/measure with the study whose finding is re-tested, and says judge relationship not labels/citationfrequency. Does the present design re-test each named earlier empirical benchmark, or merely use those works as genericbackground while re-testing Amsterdam alone? Examine authors intended finding, citation scope and actual design. Do not infer targets merely from topical similarity and do not automatically favor parent,blindcoder or priorreview. Keller cross-cultural studies (targets8–9) are outside this objection and remain settled.
